headline: Three days to the start line and the taper has held clean. Legs are fresh, engine banked, strength live to the end. From here it's 580 km on foot.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The picture is exactly what a well-executed pre-crossing quiet should look like. Recent running has been short, easy, and HR-obedient — every outing sitting low with no wandering into hard territory, which is the point right now. Strength stayed live into early this month, an unbroken run of functional sessions rather than an abrupt cutoff, so nothing was banked and then abandoned. Step counts remain high on the days they're tracked, a reminder that background movement never really stops even in a taper. The volume math still reads as a big recent build over the prior block, but that's history now — the last week deliberately steps off the gas. The one caveat worth holding lightly: the strain-tolerance status flags detraining, which is what a rolling load average does when you taper hard, not a real fitness signal. Everything here says freshness, not decline.
sections.trends: Year to date, the running is dramatically ahead of the same point last year, and the 12-week shape shows a genuine build into the last month before this deliberate step-down. That's a coherent arc: load accumulated, durability banked, then a clean unloading window ahead of a multi-day self-supported effort. The shape makes sense precisely because this athlete isn't strictly periodising — the year-round base is what makes a 580 km crossing plausible off a taper rather than a specialised peak. Nothing here reads as plateau or drift; it reads as a base deliberately parked in a ready state.
sections.threshold: Threshold pace has been stable at its current mark for the full 30-day window — no movement, but no erosion either, which is the honest read on a block that hasn't been chasing threshold. The most recent hard evidence is the long tempo-heavy effort in late July, where a substantial chunk of time sat in Z3 and Z4 at a strong pace — that's the engine confirming itself intact well before the taper quieted everything down. For what's ahead, raw threshold isn't the currency; sustained low-intensity durability under a pack is. The aerobic ceiling is demonstrably in place and doesn't need to be re-proven this week.
sections.zones: The recent distribution is exactly what a taper wants — the last several runs sit almost entirely in Z1 and Z2, with max HRs staying capped and no grey-zone creep. The per-session shapes back this up: the early-August runs are genuinely easy from start to finish, not easy-averages hiding hard surges. The one session that carried real intensity was the long July effort with meaningful Z3/Z4 time, and that was appropriately placed before the quiet began. For the intent of this window — freshen without detraining — the intensity distribution is clean and correctly weighted toward the bottom of the range.
sections.hr_comparison: Strength sessions in the most recent block don't carry HR data, so there's nothing new to read there beyond the earlier functional sessions, which sat sensibly low with only brief excursions above easy — consistent with strength work rather than conditioning-under-load. On the running side the HR sources agree with each other in trend and character; where a run recorded no chest-strap data the estimate lines up with the surrounding sessions rather than standing out. Nothing anomalous in the HR picture worth flagging.
sections.calendar: The frequency pattern in the run-up shows something worth naming: clusters of short doubles and closely-spaced easy runs rather than the spread-out rhythm of a normal training week. That's the signature of a taper being actively managed — keeping the legs turning over frequently at low cost rather than going quiet entirely. Strength cadence stayed regular right up to the edge too. The consistency here isn't about volume; it's about maintaining daily movement rhythm into the start, which is the right instinct before a multi-day effort.
sections.personal_bests: None of the speed PBs are in play this week and shouldn't be — the current focus is the opposite end of the spectrum. The most relevant record is the 50K/longest-effort mark, and the crossing ahead dwarfs it in cumulative terms; over the coming days the real story will be back-to-back durability under load, not any single-run best. Expect the PB table to stay static and read that as focus, not stagnation.

watch_items: Watch how easy-run HR behaves once loaded days start stacking under a pack — the first days will redefine what "easy" costs.
Track the back-to-back leg response early; cumulative durability under load remains the genuine unknown, not the engine.
Read the border mountain crossing as its own terrain spike, separate from the flatter coastal sections.
Watch whether nightly recovery settles once the trail rhythm replaces the travel-and-logistics window.
